questions.title: Which empty rooms are being heated anyway?
questions.why: Brick says which sensor reads which room and what the setpoint is; the scene says where the room is. A room at least 1 K over setpoint with nobody in it is energy paid for nothing, and it turns red on the plan.
questions.sparql:
SELECT ?o ?room ?temp ?setpoint WHERE {
  ?ts a brick:Zone_Air_Temperature_Sensor ; brick:hasLocation ?r ; brick:value ?temp .
  ?os a brick:Occupancy_Sensor ; brick:hasLocation ?r ; brick:value 0 .
  ?vav brick:feeds/brick:hasPart ?r ; brick:hasPoint ?sp . ?sp a brick:Zone_Air_Temperature_Setpoint ; brick:value ?setpoint .
  ?r rdfs:label ?room ; twin:depictedBy ?o .
  FILTER(?temp >= ?setpoint + 1)
} ORDER BY ?room

questions.title: If air handler 1 trips, what loses air?
questions.why: The air path (AHU feeds VAV feeds zone, which contains the room) lives only in Brick. Walked as a path, it lights the boxes and rooms that go warm, before the complaint calls start.

questions.title: Which rooms are more than 2 K off setpoint?
questions.why: Comfort complaints, found before they are made. The answer is a heat map of the floor, warm and cold together.

inference.title: Which rooms does each air handler serve?
inference.why: Brick's feeds is a chain: air handler, VAV box, zone. One rule closes the chain, and every room lights in the colour of the unit that serves it.

fault_text: Room 303's temperature sensor is mounted in Room 304, and Room 306's temperature point has been deleted from the model.
